title: Apple Applies for Preliminary Injunction to Keep OpenAI and Two Former Employees Out of Trade Secrets

content_html:
Apple has taken the battle to court. According to Gelonghui on August 4, Apple has filed a preliminary injunction request with a U.S. judge, asking the court to directly prohibit two former employees and OpenAI from accessing, obtaining, using, or disclosing so-called confidential information. Meanwhile, this trade secret lawsuit continues to progress.

The trigger came last month: Apple formally sued OpenAI and two former employees who are now working at OpenAI, accusing them of stealing Apple's trade secrets to help OpenAI enter the consumer hardware market. This lawsuit has pushed the previously under-the-surface tension between the two companies into the open, abruptly escalating the confrontation. Now applying for a preliminary injunction means Apple does not want to wait for the long trial process to conclude, but instead wants to legally restrain the other party's actions—welding shut the possible leak of confidential information before the case is resolved.

content_html_zh:
苹果已将这场官司告上法庭。 据格隆汇8月4日报道，苹果已向美国法官提出初步禁令请求，要求法院直接禁止两名前员工和OpenAI访问、获取、使用或披露所谓机密信息。 与此同时，这起商业秘密诉讼仍在继续取得进展。

导火索出现在上个月：苹果正式起诉 OpenAI 和两名现在在 OpenAI 工作的前员工，指控他们窃取苹果的商业机密，以帮助 OpenAI 进入消费硬件市场。 这起诉讼将两家公司之间原本隐藏的紧张关系推向了公开化，使对抗骤然升级。 现在申请初步禁令，意味着苹果不想等待漫长的审判过程结束，而是想在法律上约束对方的行为——在案件解决之前堵住可能泄露机密信息的可能性。
